findings.problem: BatchWorkflow carries workflow status as a plain String, allowing any value ("sent", "pending", "foo", "", null-bytes) instead of a closed domain set
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code cannot exhaustively match status; invalid strings silently pass through; serialization of unknown states corrupts downstream consumers
findings.fix: Replace with a sealed enum: pub enum BatchStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } and remove is_validated/is_sent booleans

findings.problem: No typestate type is used; the struct has no compile-time guarantee that transitions follow a valid order (e.g. validated before sent). mark_sent can be called without prior validation
findings.failure_mode: A batch can be marked sent without ever being validated, violating the workflow invariant; any code path that calls mark_sent directly bypasses the validation gate with zero compiler warning
findings.fix: Introduce a typestate enum or GADT-style wrapper (e.g. BatchWorkflow<S> where S: State) so that mark_sent only accepts a validated-typestate token, making unvalidated-sent a compile error

findings.problem: is_validated is a standalone boolean encoding part of the lifecycle; combined with is_sent, it allows 4 logical states but only 3 are valid, and the struct name itself signals invalid states exist
findings.failure_mode: is_validated=false, is_sent=true becomes an impossible but representable state (batch sent without validation); is_validated=true, is_sent=true loses information about which happened first
findings.fix: Fold lifecycle flags into a single enum: pub enum BatchLifecycle { New, Validated, Sent { sent_at_ms: u64 } }

findings.problem: is_sent is a standalone boolean encoding part of the lifecycle; duplicates information already partially in status String, and is inconsistent with is_validated
findings.failure_mode: is_sent=true but status!="sent" becomes a silent invariant violation; callers must check both fields leading to bugs where one is updated and the other is not
findings.fix: Remove is_sent entirely; it is redundant with the lifecycle enum variant and the sent_at_epoch_ms field

findings.problem: Optional lifecycle data is detached from the lifecycle state; sent_at_epoch_ms is None when is_sent=true is a valid state (early before clock read) and Some(...) when is_sent=false is an invariant violation
findings.failure_mode: A batch with is_sent=false and sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(12345) is representable but violates the invariant that sent timestamps only exist for sent batches
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant of the lifecycle enum so Some is only possible when in the Sent state

findings.problem: BatchWorkflow id is a raw String with no domain semantics; any string is accepted as a valid batch ID with no length, format, or uniqueness validation at the boundary
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, whitespace-only strings, or overly long IDs are accepted as valid batch identifiers; downstream sorting or hashing treats the raw bytes as domain keys without validation
findings.fix: Replace with a newtype: pub struct BatchId(String) or pub struct BatchId(#[deny(dead_code)] [u8; N]) with a smart constructor that validates the id on creation and returns a typed error

findings.construct: pub fn mark_sent(mut item: BatchWorkflow) -> BatchWorkflow
findings.problem: mark_sent accepts any BatchWorkflow regardless of its current state; there is no check that is_validated=true or status=="validated" before allowing the sent transition
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can invoke mark_sent on a brand-new, unvalidated batch and it will silently transition it to sent status with is_sent=true, completely bypassing the validation step
findings.fix: Signature must require a validated token: pub fn mark_sent(item: BatchWorkflow<Validated>) -> BatchWorkflow<Sent> or at minimum check is_validated and return Result, failing the transition if false

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent throughput or allocation behavior
no profiler evidence showing mark_sent hot-path cost
no allocation evidence: .to_string() on every mark_sent call creates an unnecessary heap allocation for the literal "sent"

residual_risk: Static review of a 13-line crate with 7 BLOCKER findings. No commands were executed. The struct cannot compile a correct typestate machine without structural refactoring; all lifecycle transitions are unguarded. Fix requires enum-based typestate, removal of status String, elimination of lifecycle booleans, newtype for ID, and guarded transition functions.
